title: Sable and the Ledger
premise: Ansel Thornbury, the reclusive archivist of St. Verrine's Cathedral, is cataloguing the effects of a missing parishioner, Mara Quill, when he finds her diary continues writing entries for weeks after her disappearance. Following the diary's coded references into the locked crypt, Ansel uncovers a ledger of secret payments implicating the cathedral's beloved dean in Mara's staged disappearance—she fled an arranged marriage and a cover-up of stolen restoration funds, hiding in plain sight among the cathedral's night staff. As the anniversary dinner approaches and the dean moves to destroy the ledger, Ansel must choose between his duty of silence and the found family of misfits who've quietly adopted him; he exposes the truth at the dinner itself, and Mara, who has been watching him all along, steps out of the shadows to reclaim her name.
about_author: J. M. Marchetti is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade among ledgers, crypts, and the small dramas of cathedral life. They write mysteries about quiet people forced into loud courage.

chapters.title: The Weight of Dust
chapters.summary: Ansel Thornbury, the cathedral's invisible archivist, is assigned to catalogue the belongings of Mara Quill, missing seven months and presumed dead. In her flat he finds a diary whose final entry is dated three weeks after her disappearance. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: unease stirring in a man who prefers the company of paper to people.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Ansel reads the impossible entries in secret, learning Mara wrote in code about 'the glass ledger' and someone called 'the Shepherd.' The night custodian, Odile, notices his distraction and draws him into the staff's late-night tea circle. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: the first crack in his isolation—a found family forming without his permission.

chapters.title: Beneath the Flagstones
chapters.summary: Following the diary's references to 'the room below the singing,' Ansel picks the lock of the crypt and finds a hidden alcove containing a financial ledger of unrecorded donations. Someone has been in the crypt recently; the dust is disturbed. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: dread mixed with the thrill of purpose.

chapters.title: The Shepherd's Voice
chapters.summary: The ledger traces to Dean Halloway, the cathedral's beloved shepherd. Ansel confronts the organist, Tobias, who admits Mara discovered Halloway was skimming restoration funds and helped her vanish to protect her from Halloway's rage. POV: Ansel, with a flashback to Mara's diary voice. Emotional beat: loyalty to the dead curdling into suspicion of the living.

chapters.title: What Odile Knows
chapters.summary: Ansel shares his findings with Odile, who reveals she saw a woman in the cloister at night—alive, wearing a staff coat—and has said nothing for months. The anniversary dinner for Mara is announced for Sunday. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: hope, terrifying because it means Mara may be in danger still.

chapters.title: A Page Torn Out
chapters.summary: Ansel returns to the crypt and finds the ledger gone; in its place, a torn diary page addressed to him by name. Halloway invites Ansel to his office, offering a promotion and a gentle warning about 'unsettled ghosts.' POV: Ansel, with Halloway's POV interlude. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing he has become the hunted.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Glass
chapters.summary: Ansel reconstructs the missing page from memory and diary marginalia: Mara hid a duplicate of the ledger inside the dinner's commemorative chalice, commissioned before she vanished. Tobias confesses Halloway ordered the chalice melted. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: grief for the found family's complicity in silence.

chapters.title: Night of Bells
chapters.summary: Ansel and Odile break into the foundry the night before the dinner and recover the chalice's inner lining—the duplicate ledger, intact. Halloway's warden catches them; they barely escape through the bell tower as the midnight bells cover their flight. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve; he is no longer invisible and no longer wishes to be.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: At the anniversary dinner, Ansel rises during the toast and reads the ledger aloud, accusing Halloway before the congregation. Halloway denies everything—until Mara herself walks in, alive, holding the original diary, and names the account numbers from memory. POV: Ansel and Mara in alternating sections. Emotional beat: the climax—truth spoken in the one room that swore to silence.

chapters.title: A Name Reclaimed
chapters.summary: Halloway is arrested; the parish reels, then slowly forgives the staff who stayed quiet out of fear. Mara asks Ansel why he kept reading, and he admits he wanted, for once, to be needed. The tea circle sets a fourth cup at the table. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: belonging, finally, on purpose.
